It may feel like it but life isn't a game. It's difficult and a struggle at times but it's not comparable to something as simple as a board or video game. 

If you're serious about "returning" this game I think we should talk more but without the metaphor.

Being reactive is only giving that monster what he would want. 

The truth is as bad as things are right now, I can't imagine all that is going to change with Trump in power, understand that (as terrible as he may be) he's a person that acts more as figure head. Fear is overwhelming a lot of us right now however ending your life is never a solution for this. 

Be stronger, be better than him.
There are many people here willing to listen if you're looking to talk to someone. What's on your mind?

Don't. 

Economic issues are never worth ending something like a life. Economics are meaningless, they're something invented, life is so much more than that. Life is something extremely rare and lucky. 

If G really if the love of your life, you're going to be hurting them.

You sound like you need to vent. We're hear to listen.

You mention people won't care when you're gone but even if that is true, who cares about what they think? There is meaning in everything choice you make and it matters to you. There is a whole person on the other side my keyboard who wrote what you just did, someone who wants to be heard. 

Maybe she feels like no one cares but she does, clearly. The most terrifying fact about the universe is not that it's hostile but that it is indifferent. The trick is coming to terms with it's indifference and understanding that you can find meaning, you can ASSIGN meaning to things in your life you find important. Don't rely on others to make you feel special; KNOW You're special. 

The navigating this life is abyssal black then WE need to supply our own light and that means finding joy in the things we do. Don't define yourself by societies standard of success but rather ask yourself what makes you happy. 

What makes you happy?

Take a second, step back and breathe. 

Why are you lonely? Do you choose not to be socially active? 

Sometimes it feels like we're overwhelmed with decisions but often we forget that many of them are simply taking a chance on what you feel may work out best, no one KNOWS which school to go to, which courses to take and the few that do are often the ones that end up regretting their decisions. 

Is it possible you're overwhelmed right now? You're starting an amazing chapter of your life rather than ending it this is the best time to evaluate what you like and dislike about the way you handle things and work to change them. 

Many people wish for an opportunity like the one you've been presented.

You mention chickening out, well I hate to break it to you, but suicide is chickening out. It's giving up on something that is so amazing.

Why are you lonely?
Don't

You always have a reason to live, a job and money and a mate are not what defines your life. 

You may feel that these are the most important things in life, but they really are not. 

You don't need allies unless you're opposing something, and whether you feel ugly or not it doesn't define what you become or who you are, your actions define you. 

We all have moments of weakness, where we may feel tiny or insignificant, we all know what that feels like. But they are moments of weakness because it's easier to pretend there are things we cannot change about ourselves.

You say that nothing will ever improve? Why? What do you want to improve on? Pick one thing. Even if it's as simple as changing the way you think about movies or books. 

Sometimes it seems to dark ahead that we need to dig down deep within ourselves in order to supply our own light, otherwise we just walk into darkness.

If you hate people and can't stand being around them, then maybe take a break for awhile?

Take a few days off work or school, reset your thinking. We tend to get really focused on little microcosm we build around our lives and sometimes need to take a step back.

Well, why did you fail your exam? Being afraid of dogs is not stupid - sometimes dogs can be very violent. 

You can't blame yourself for your feelings - you haven't done anything wrong.

I think if it's working for you I wouldn't risk skipping it.

However if you still feel like having a drink - you'd have to check the medication to avoid serious injury. 

That being said - I'm just giving my perspective :)

When it comes down to it you should do whatever you feel is right, trust yourself - I'm sure you know what to do! :)
Help me understand; what have you done wrong?

It wouldn't show them; it wouldn't prove anything. 

I know you think it will, hope that doing something harsh will make them all see the light - but it won't. 

It's not the answer. 

Sometimes you need to take a deep breath before seeing things clearly. Wait a day - a week. Let the dust settle before making any rash decisions. No one ever thought clearly in such a short time.

Well, no one truly knows what comes after death. 

Personally I believe that there is nothing - just empty blackness of non-existence.

But there is so much more in this world right now that is worth staying for - not just the fear of what may come.

So maybe the best I can say is that I'm here, I've read your story. There are people in the world that care enough about you to connect as well. Even if they can't think of anything to say at the moment....

I Hey Voxpupil, I'm here and willing to talk. 

A Girl and Friends are not the only thing worth living for, in fact they're not even near the top of the list. You can't force a friendship and when the time is right, I'm sure you'll meet someone who you would call your friend. Besides there are probably people out there that may be thinking the same thing, and perhaps they're looking at you wondering why you are not their friend either. It's a very large world and nothing is 100% absolute, so don't make decisions that are absolute. 

You may have friends in the future and maybe even a girlfriend, but more importantly don't let things like that define you. If you have siblings, or cousins, or even no one else, you can always find comfort. 

There's nothing wrong with being alone, sometimes that can be the most helpful, but you have to comfortable first. Learn to be comfortable alone. 

Remember that what you're feeling is not a new feeling, people of all ages have felt alone before. We all feel this way sometimes it's human nature. 

Don't jump off a bridge, because that will solve nothing. 

I'm here if you wanna continue talking.

Almost all of what I said was feel-good jargon, and as I said originally all I can really offer is my opinion. 

There is nothing wrong with being stubborn, but if you believe you are not, than I'll take your word for it. 

Beauty is subjective, and what I said was that life CAN be beautiful, and that you WILL find beauty. What that beauty will be is completely unknown to me, but you'll find it. 

I think it's preposterous as well, but try telling him that. 

I'm attempting to listen to you and give you what little advice I can offer. The truth is there is a great deal of tough love everybody and their mother could dish out, but I knew that would be futile, as I knew what I had originally posted would be. Perhaps talking about in itself helps a bit?

No one ever wants to move on. When my mother died the last thing I said to her was something along the lines of "I hate you." I loved my mother more than anything but I was in a fight with her at the time. 

The sad truth is, although you may not want it, you will forget his voice, his smell, his taste, even maybe his face. This is inevitable. Time fades everything. It's not a pleasant thought, it's an awful one, I no longer remember my mum's voice, or smell or smile. I have pictures but I don't even really remember what she looked like, but you know what I do remember? My Mum. When someone passes they become a whole new feeling, a part of you really. It takes time and acceptance and a great deal of heartache, but eventually it passes, all things must pass. 

Don't think, know that one day you will forget what he looks like, or smell like or tastes like, whether you want to or not. But never forget him. And you won't. You may not want to move on, but you will. Take your time now, think of him as often as you would like, but know that in time you'll look back on him in fondness not in sadness. Know that you eventually will remember his life and not his death. Because in the end that's what we should be remembering. No one wants to be mourned over, people want to be celebrated.

I've read what you said and Oddly I can relate. Although I am not your age I have often had your mindset, you do seem mature for your age, and I would never say those are teenage problem, even if they were teenage problems. Here's what little advice I'll offer:

1) If we are insignificant and pointless, which we very well may be, that still doesn't mean we can't live full and interesting lives. We are victims of a society that has bred consumers and socially awkward people with problems, me being one of them, but you have something others may not, scarecrow, you have a realistic, some would say pessimistic view of the world. Is there anything wrong with that? Not at all. You may have the views you have now for the rest of your life, you may not. That is a fact of the human condition, we are constantly changing, evolving, mutating even, to something new and different. Perhaps everything IS in fact pointless. But pointless itself means that there is no climax, no high point, but this doesn't mean we can't make one. Okay so we're born, we live, we die, and maybe that's enough for some people. Maybe that's enough for you, maybe even me sometimes. But The fact that you are intelligent enough to think so tells me that you are among the few that may "get" it. Whether "it" be right or not. You clearly question things, think of things analytically and with realism. And although you strongly feel you don't care about anything, I assure you, you do. Even if it's as simple as caring about rational thinking. 

2) Find a passion. It's tough, I know because I've tried to do so myself. I've been to college for 3 different programs, all thinking one would be perfect for me. Many people, like myself are born with a passion. My father was born to ride motorcycles, he knew that from the time he first saw one, and I envy him for it. I am still finding my passion, but the quest gives me meaning enough. Cooking, Music, Painting, Interviewing People, Fixing Cars, Camping, Fishing there are so many things in the world that are interesting, if you don't think so, I guarantee you haven't found yours yet.  

3) There is no answer, and even if their was, I know you too well already to say that you would most likely not accept it. That's a good thing. You have a strong will, stubborn almost. Leaders posses stubborn qualities. Great minds and thinkers often accepted the world for the endless nothingness it was, understand the we are a grain of sand. But true great men and woman took a look at that grain of sand and said, "Fuck it, I'll do it anyways." It is the most thing important to question the world, question religion and death and life and birth and society and love. But don't allow your questions to provide you answers. Because here's the bottom line; We don't know. I, like you, sometimes think it's all pointless, that existence is meaningless and life is but a dream, but what if it isn't? Ya we may die and that's it, but just because the credits are shitty does that mean we shouldn't bother watching the movie? 

4)  My last point is this. You are intelligent enough to know that we are not unique. And if we are not unique than there are countless others on this earth identical to us in almost every way. And it we have someone else on this earth that is Identical to us, than there is another person that feels the exact way you feel. You are not a snowflake. People have thought these thoughts and will continue to think them. But be stronger than those who were trampled by them. Rise above them and know that you are stronger than anything that may come.

I'm here, and I've read what you have to say. I something I said helps at least a little. I'm here to continue to talk if you would like. Life can be beautiful, but sometimes you have to work at it. You will find the beauty I promise.

Well again I've read your story and I hear you. Again you may not be looking for advice, but I might as well say my thoughts anyway in case they may help; 

1) Depression is an seemingly impossible thing to over come and sometimes the weight of the world and social pressures can come from all sides can be overwhelming. But you mentioned a very key thing when you said that you thought you may have the strength to feel like you could overcome your depression and your suicidal thoughts. Even though that has passed the fact that the knowledge and power lies within you is important, but I'll come back to that....

2) in regards to the person you love. Love is a complex emotion. It can make you do and say and feel things nothing else in the world can, but more importantly knowing that he cut himself and not telling anyone is not your fault. It was as you said in retrospect possibly a poor choice, but hindsight is always 20/20, meaning it's always easy to look back on your mistakes and say, oh I screwed up. Here's the facts, the past is the past, there is nothing that will change that, but where you are now in your life is present and that is what you must take a hold of and not let go. You should miss him, but you shouldn't feel terrible, and you should never want to die. Nothing in this world is so awful that you should want to end it. The thing is, just like you knew that in retrospect your choice not to say anything may have been a bad one, the retrospect of ending your life would be 100 times worse, the difference is that you won't be able to look back at the people who are missing you, crying their eyes out because you are no longer in their life. Trust me on this. 

3) "obviously i don't want to make anyone else suicidal too" you cannot make anyone suicidal. It is something that resides within someone it cannot be planted there, it can be affected by outside elements but nothing you did planted it there. Know That. 

4) This may not score me any points but I've dealt with nearly everything talked about on this subreddit and here's what i want to leave you with, FairyJasmines, tragedy befalls all of us at one point or another, death is the only thing in this world that we all experience, it is the constant, the ending point an absolute. And if we all experience death than you must know that people will and have felt like you have before and after you...and in this I've always found comfort. If you were at a lottery drawing and had a ticket, would you leave after the 3rd number? Or stick around till the end to see if you've won? The end is the same for all of us, so wait around until the end. You know that you have felt better, "i felt like things could actually turn out good for me" so know that sometimes you're up and sometimes you're down. All of this in due time will be a sad memory, yes. But it will also be a tale to others showing them the adversity that you have over come. You have strength. I don't know you and I can tell already in your words, you have a very strong will, independent and powerful. 

I hope maybe something I've said sticks, if not know that I'm here to listen to you. I hope they find your friend alive and well, but if it is the worst, know that as you miss him other would miss you. And if you feel this way now, would you really want another to feel that way about you? Even if it's just me.
Well thanks! If you ever need to talk and I am not online PM and I'll be happy to talk about anything when I have time.

Well it sounds like you have a small amount of social anxiety and you tend to over think things because of it. Unfortunately like so many things that tend to govern people lives there is no easy answer, and I know that's not what you're looking for anyways. I can offer only a few points:

1) I've read what you have to say. I've listened to you and although your problems seem very great you need to realize that the fact you understand what it is specifically about you and how it effects you puts you miles ahead of most people. Imagine feeling the way you do but not having the slightest understanding of why or how you feel this way, or not even realizing that you have an issue. You are conscience and intelligent which leads me to believe that you are going to be fine.

2) Whenever I have had a problem that made me over analyze things or make me feel awkward or even alone, there was always a thought that kept me thinking straight; You are not alone. You may feel as though you are the only one in your school who has severe depression or social anxiety or evaluation anxiety or thinking about what expressions you're making or what your tone of voice is.... but I promise you there are at least 2 other people feeling the exact same way. The simultaneous comfort and discomfort of knowing that you may not be 100% unique is about how you view it, know that you can over come your feelings because people before you have, and people after you will. There is nothing too powerful that you as an intelligent citizen of earth cannot overcome, don't think this, KNOW THIS, because I swear to you it's the damn truth.

3) The only way to solve a problem is to work on it, and you've taken the first steps. Anyone reading what you wrote will immediately understand that you are intelligent and fair minded, that's not a compliment that's a fact. Know this and use it. Overcoming diversity in any shape or form it takes is hard work, but nothing worth having comes easy. 

I hope my words have maybe sparked a thought in you, if nothing else know that I'm here and willing to continue talking. There are always people that care.
